delivered.writer: SQLiteEventJournalWriter: one private validatedIdentity body (schema parse, canonical command identity, duplicate eventId) now shared by appendWithExtension, appendPreparedWithExtension and the new synchronous appendInBorrowedTransaction, which requires db.inTransaction, never begins/commits/notifies. appendWithExtension takes an optional onCommitted, called with the extension result after its own .immediate() COMMIT returned and before the promise settles; a notification request inside a caller transaction (where the wrapper is only a SAVEPOINT) is refused before writing. rejectPreparedThenable is exported unchanged
delivered.storeContract: ICampaignEventStore: ICampaignAppendRefusal {kind:refused, reason}, CAMPAIGN_APPEND_CONTROLS_UNSUPPORTED, ICampaignCommittedBatch (plain identity), ICampaignAppendControls {guard?, onCommitted?}, CampaignControlledBatchResult, and the explicit optional capability appendControlledCommandBatch. InMemoryCampaignEventStore is untouched and therefore not guard-capable
delivered.adapter: JournalCampaignEventStore: appendCampaignCommandBatch keeps its exported signature (thin wrapper, six outside callers unchanged) over the in-place body now named appendControlledCampaignBatch. On a SQLite writer the guard runs on the transaction handle after the recorded-id check and before append(); a refusal returns before any write; thenables are rejected; the saved-record afterCommit hook still runs inside SQL after the append (rollback-capable); a frozen committed identity is built inside the transaction and onCommitted fires from the writer after COMMIT with its throw captured as notificationError. Non-SQLite journal + any control: typed append-controls-unsupported refusal before any write. The class keeps branch-before-duplicate and prior-receipt order for both appendCommandBatch and appendControlledCommandBatch, so a genuine duplicate is never guarded, notified or refused
delivered.host: campaignHostBatchCommit: CampaignCommitOutcome gains refused, commit-uncertain {commandId, error} and committed-unsettled {commandId, events, errors}; resultOfCommit is a switch whose default hands the remaining arms to throwCommitFailure(never), so typecheck proves no arm is dropped; append rejection -> commit-uncertain (projection untouched, nothing published); after a known commit the notification error, divergence, rebuild failure and each publish failure are collected in order and the batch is never compensated. CampaignMatchHost.doors: CampaignDoorOutcome (answered | commit outcome), resultOfDoor, controls threaded through commitEvents/commitValidated/applyHostIntentLocked, openLocked now maps failures instead of dropping them. CampaignMatchHost: commitEvents refuses guard/onCommitted before the first event when the store lacks appendControlledCommandBatch (plain batch store and per-event fallback); new door applyHostIntentWithControls (same lock/replay/validation/identity order) answers with the classified outcome and runs afterRelease once after the single-writer lock is released; publish now delivers to every subscriber before rethrowing; announceMissionLaunched and _commitEventsForTests use throwCommitFailure

behaviourChanges: Uncontrolled doors keep their CampaignIntentResult contract and still throw the same error object for a single failure (e.g. CampaignProjectionDivergenceError); with several post-commit failures they now throw an AggregateError of all of them instead of only the first

CampaignMatchHost.publish delivers an event to every subscriber even when one throws, then rethrows (single error as-is, several as AggregateError); previously the first throwing subscriber stopped delivery to the rest
After a verification divergence whose rebuild also fails, the divergence error is kept alongside the rebuild error (previously the rebuild error replaced it)
openLocked previously ignored the commit outcome value; failures were already thrown and still are
designNotes: commit-uncertain leaves the live projection untouched (as today) rather than re-reading it from the journal. A re-read was tried and reverted: it changed the existing campaignHostSerialization "keeps serving doors after one of them throws" case, whose poisoned store makes the next door validate against the pre-failure projection. Readback/recovery of an uncertain command is left to the owner via the carried commandId (the uncertain-readback pipeline case shows it)

afterRelease failure: on committed it yields committed-unsettled (commandId from the intent identity, null when the intent offered none); on committed-unsettled it is appended to errors; on any other outcome the door throws an AggregateError carrying the outcome as cause; on a thrown door it is aggregated with the original error
A refusal can only be produced on the controlled path; resultOfCommit/throwCommitFailure throw if one ever reaches an uncontrolled door (fail closed, never success)
